text_to_speech: Hello astronomers! Many of you know one of the biggest problems in modern astrophotography is cable management. Today I want to show you how the EAGLE, thanks to the all-in-one design, provides the best solution, by reducing number and length of cables needed for your telescope. Let’s start! A telescope setup for astrophotography uses many devices that have to be powered and controlled from a computer: mount, camera, focuser, autoguider, filter wheel, dew heaters, etc. This means we’ll have a lot of data and power cables all around your telescope! And every device will need to be powered separately, so you will have also many power units. If you use a standard computer to control all of these devices, when the telescope moves by slewing and tracking astronomical objects, all these cables may pull and, in the worst case, disconnect. That's why we designed the EAGLE not only to be the best computer to remotely control your telescope but also to improve cable management. This way all your devices in your telescope are connected and powered through the EAGLE with less and shorter cables. And all of them are powered with a single power in cable from your battery or power unit. This way the telescope is free to move any part of the sky and track all night long because cables will move together with the telescope and they won’t pull or detach. That's why the EAGLE is the solution for a better cable management in telescopes and astrophotography. For more content that will help you to explore the universe like a pro, subscribe to our channel and clear skies!

youtube_description:
Cable management in an astrophotography telescope is very difficult as it is necessary to use many devices (mount, camera, autoguider, electronic focuser, motorized filter wheel, etc.) that require data and power cables. If you connect all of these devices to a standard external computer, when the telescope moves, cables may pull or disconnect. Instead, by using the EAGLE, you can simplify cable management: you will need less and shorter cables that will move together with your telescope.

Discover more in our website https://www.primalucelab.com/astronomy/blog/gestione-dei-cavi-in-astrofotografia-con-eagle-astrophotography-cable-management/
